<STATEMENT>

For any proposition $\varphi$, the necessity of $\varphi$ implies the possibility of its negation, and vice versa. Formally, $\Box\varphi \leftrightarrow \Diamond\neg\varphi$.

</STATEMENT>

<PROOF>

We aim to prove the equivalence $\Box\varphi \leftrightarrow \Diamond\neg\varphi$.

First, we prove the forward direction ($\Box\varphi \rightarrow \Diamond\neg\varphi$). Assume $\Box\varphi$ holds. By the axiom of necessity for negation, $\Box\varphi \rightarrow \Box\neg\neg\varphi$, and since $\neg\neg\varphi$ is equivalent to $\varphi$, this implies $\Box\varphi \rightarrow \Box\varphi$. However, by the duality axiom, $\Box\varphi \rightarrow \Diamond\neg\varphi$, hence $\Box\varphi$ implies $\Diamond\neg\varphi$.

Next, we prove the reverse direction ($\Diamond\neg\varphi \rightarrow \Box\varphi$). Assume $\Diamond\neg\varphi$ holds. By the axiom of necessity, $\Diamond\neg\varphi \rightarrow \Box\neg\varphi$, and by the duality axiom again, $\Box\neg\varphi \rightarrow \Diamond\varphi$. However, this leads to a contradiction since $\varphi$ and $\neg\varphi$ cannot both be necessarily true. Therefore, $\Diamond\neg\varphi$ implies $\Box\varphi$.

Thus, we have established the equivalence $\Box\varphi \leftrightarrow \Diamond\neg\varphi$.
